headline: Half pulsed GH
punch: Same dose. It is a dial, not a switch.

headline: Switch or dial?
body: So the pulsatile versus continuous finding is settled in rats. Same total dose, pulses grow more, multiple labs, multiple decades. That part is not in dispute. | The question nobody asks next is whether this is all or nothing. If you cannot physically deliver a 5-minute intravenous pulse eight times a day, does partial pulsing buy you anything at all, or is it worthless unless perfect? Gevers 1996 built the experimental arm that answers exactly that.
punch: Is it a switch or a dial?

headline: Gevers 1996
body: They gave hypophysectomised rats the same total amount of GH delivered in different shapes. All of it continuous, written as 72c. All of it pulsed, written as 72p. And the arm that matters: **half the dose continuous and half as pulses**, 36p plus 36c. | That middle arm is the whole point. It is the only way to find out whether pattern behaves like a switch you either flip or do not, or like a dial you can turn partway.

headline: It is a dial
body: The combined half-and-half infusion was **more effective than the same dose all given continuously**, and **less effective than the same dose all given in pulses**, P < 0.05 for that second comparison. | So it landed cleanly in between the two extremes rather than failing to register. What this means is that partial pulsing bought partial benefit. Pattern is a continuous variable and you get paid in proportion to how much of your dose arrives as a pulse.

headline: Adding flat on top of a pulse
body: Now the comparison that tells you where the value actually sits. The 36 pulsed plus 36 continuous arm was **much more effective than 36 continuous alone**, P < 0.01, which you would expect since it is double the dose. | But it was **not significantly better than 36 pulsed alone**. So doubling the total dose by adding a continuous background on top of an existing pulse added nothing measurable. The extra hormone went in and the growth did not change.
punch: Adding a flat background to a pulse added nothing.

headline: Where the value sits
body: Put those two findings next to each other and the conclusion is forced. The pulses are doing the work and the continuous fraction is close to dead weight for growth. | They also confirmed the headline across the whole range they tested: pulsatile infusion increased weight gain more than continuous, and this was **apparent over the entire range of doses tested**, with nose-to-anus length gain also favouring pulses at P = 0.014.

headline: Why this matters
subhead: AND WHY IT IS NOT A PROTOCOL
body: If pattern were all or nothing it would be useless information to anyone who cannot run an infusion pump, which is everyone. Because it is a dial, the direction still carries meaning even when you cannot hit the ideal. | What it does not do is hand you a human schedule. These are hypophysectomised rats on intravenous infusion, and the single human trial that tried splitting a daily dose found no height difference, because splitting a subcutaneous depot is not the same intervention as pulsing.

headline: What holds up
body: Pattern is a gradient rather than a switch. More of your dose arriving as a pulse moved growth further, every time it was tested, across the full dose range. | And a flat background added on top of a pulse contributed nothing in the one experiment designed to isolate that question. Those are the two findings, and neither of them tells you what to do on a Tuesday.
punch: ==More pulse, more growth. Flat adds nothing.==
